newsitem.title: BELGIUM: PetroFina bucks falling Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: PetroFina bucks falling Brussels bourse.

text.p: Belgian oil and gas group PetroFina bucked a falling Brussels bourse on Wednesday as investors welcomed news of a 38 percent rise in 1996 earnings.
But analysts were mixed as to whether the share would maintain the upward momentum in coming weeks.
In a provisional earnings statement on Tuesday, PetroFina said 1996 net profit rose to around 16.0 billion Belgian francs from 11.6 billion in 1995, exceeding most expectations.
The news helped lift PetroFina's shares 2.2 percent in early bourse trade on Wednesday. By 1400 GMT the share was still up 0.9 percent at 11,450 francs while most other shares were lower.

"The results were definitely better than expected," Bank Degroof analyst Caroline Lauwers told Reuters. She said she had raised her 1996 earnings estimate to around 680 francs from 650 francs a share and now pegged 1997 earnings at about 780 francs.

Generale Bank analyst Sandra Vandersmissen said she now estimated 1996 earnings at 700 francs, up from 630 francs - which had been near the consensus. Earnings per share could rise 13 percent to 790 francs in 1997, she said.
Both analysts expected the company, when it releases final figures in March, to announce a sharply higher net dividend, with Lauwers estimating 300 francs and Vandersmissen 345 francs.

They were divided, however, on the outlook for the company's share. Generale Bank's Vandersmissen said she expected it to show a smooth increase, noting the bank had rated PetroFina a buy since late last year.

Bank Degroof's Lauwers said, however, the share was correctly valued. "If it goes up it's just for short-term positive elements," she said. Bank Degroof had previously issued a "buy" recommendation on the share when it was at 10,900.
Both noted the company remained highly sensitive to movements in the dollar, oil prices and European refining margins.
